 Restoration Druid Rotation Guide - Midnight
 

 
 
 By Voulk

 Welcome to the Restoration Druid rotation guide for ! This guide will teach you all about the optimal rotation for Restoration Druid across its various talent builds. It will cover both core ability cadence and cooldown usage in dungeons and raids for .

Restoration Druid Rotation in Midnight

Restoration Druid is a heal-over-time-based healer that combines such effects with a large direct heal that scales off them in Regrowth. Restoration Druid has many answers to most questions dungeons will ask of you and you should feel like a very powerful healer once you've picked up the basics. It is especially well-suited to small group content. In Midnight it largely plays similarly to in The War Within. Here are a few quick tips to get you started:

 Maximize Wild Growth & Swiftmend Casts: In addition to being reasonable healing casts, both Swiftmend and Wild Growth have a ton of extra effects like spawning a Grove Guardian (which itself buffs all of our healing), Reforestation, Everbloom, Verdant Infusion and more. Swiftmend is a bigger priority, and it's fine to sit on Wild Growth if there is no damage going out.
 

 Utilize Abundance: Put Rejuvenation out on the group before or as damage hits so that your follow-up Regrowth casts are free and will always Crit. This is the heart of the Restoration Druid playstyle and most of our healing and mana efficiency starts here.
 

 Use Major Cooldowns: Cast Convoke the Spirits / Incarnation: Tree of Life and Tranquility very often. Pre-plan them before tough fights so that you can line them up with difficult moments in the fight. 

If you're looking for a more bite-sized rotation explanation, check out our simplified guide below:

Restoration Druid Beginner Guide

 Best Restoration Druid Healing Priority and Rotation

Both Restoration hero trees have a place where they are best and while we have a selector here, you will mostly find the Mythic+ section to focus on Wildstalker play and the raid section to focus on Keeper of the Grove play. You do not need to DPS in Cat Form to play Wildstalker. This is a common misconception.

 Keeper of the Grove Raid

 Wildstalker Raid

The Druid raid strategy focuses on building large windows of burst healing by stacking healing increase talents like Harmony of the Grove and Power of Nature with our healing cooldowns like Convoke the Spirits or Incarnation: Tree of Life.

Restoration Druid cooldowns are built into what we call a "ramp", where we combine our spells and cooldowns to create massive peaks of healing. A ramp is a commonly used term in the WoW community to refer to a healing pattern where you combine spells in such a way that there is a "build-up" phase and a "payoff" phase. By combining our spells in this way, we are able to get more value out of each of them, while also creating powerful burst windows that we can line up against the damage of a fight. These high-damage phases tend to be the most dangerous and likely to kill someone, and Restoration Druid has great counters to them. In Midnight, your rotation will be slightly less bursty than in recent expansions as the game turns to more consistent healing patterns.

Regardless of Hero Tree, our "build-up" phase consists mostly of Rejuvenation casts. We'll prepare by making sure Efflorescence was refreshed recently, and then we'll hit the raid with as many Rejuvenations as we can fit 10-12 seconds before we're expecting heavy damage. You'll then move to the "payoff" phase by dropping Wild Growth and big cooldowns like Convoke the Spirits. You can also hit Innervate early in your ramp to make the entire thing free. After you've hit your big cooldowns, you can complete the "payoff" phase by casting as many Regrowths as are necessary. We're taking Abundance and have a lot of Rejuvenations out, so these will actually be almost free.

If you are taking Incarnation: Tree of Life then you'll cast that before you start casting Rejuvenation since the big mana discount is a central part of its value. You can find significant discussion on Convoke the Spirits vs Incarnation: Tree of Life in the talents section of the guide.

Begin your Rejuvenation ramp ~15 seconds before damage hits.
Hit Swiftmend followed by Rejuvenation. The Swiftmend procs Soul of the Forest, which will give you two free superpowered Rejuvenation buffs on the follow-up cast.
The Swiftmend and Wild Growth casts automatically proc Grove Guardians which will significantly buff your healing.
Convoke is your short-cooldown burst heal, and it has about a 50% chance to proc a mini-Flourish which will extend your Rejuvenation buffs.

Cast Regrowth until your Abundance stacks wear off. These will have a 100% Crit chance and cost basically no mana. We'll be tracking Abundance with the cooldown manager. Each Regrowth cast will also heal everyone else with Regrowth due to the Nature's Bounty talent.
The number of Regrowth to cast here depends on the fight and your Abundance stacks. As your Rejuvenation buffs start to run out, your Regrowths will rise in cost but you'll also have more Regrowth out for Nature's Bounty value so you are usually good to continue if the raid is still taking heavy damage.

 Ramp Timing

Ramp timing depends heavily on the specifics of the fight but there are a few general rules:
Maximize how often you can cast your big cooldowns.
Try not to use them during periods of low damage.

You also have some flexibility around how you combine your cooldowns. Each is often weaker alone, but sometimes you'd prefer to hit more frequent damage windows even if it's less overall HPS. 

Keep Efflorescence active as frequently as possible. Our default build will take Lifetreading which means you will automatically keep Efflorescence active by keeping Lifebloom up.
4Lifebloom is a crucial spell to keep up at all times due to our Apex talent, Everbloom. If you Swiftmend your Lifebloom target then you won't need to refresh it manually very often (due to Verdant Infusion). If your healing is struggling then it is worth checking your Lifebloom uptime.
2Cast Swiftmend and Wild Growth on cooldown if the raid has taken any damage. Follow Swiftmend with Rejuvenation.
In between short cooldowns and maintenance spells rotate Rejuvenation and Regrowth in cycles. Cast Rejuvenation until your Abundance stacks are high and then swap to Regrowth until they are low again. Mix in Wrath casts as required for mana. Try to avoid casting Regrowth with low Abundance stacks.
7Fill any free time with Wrath. This restores quite a lot of Mana over an average fight due to Master Shapeshifter.

I'm having mana trouble 

You can never really run out of mana with the Master Shapeshifter talent since you always have a way to regenerate it. However, there is still major value in getting as much healing out of your mana as possible so that you don't have to spend as much time casting Wrath. Here are some tips to improve your mana:
Avoid casting too many Regrowths with low Abundance stacks. 
Make sure you cast Innervate on cooldown. Cast your first when you're at 80% mana and then whenever it comes back. You'll want to cast Innervate when you do not have high Abundance stacks, and you'll mostly cast Rejuvenation during it.
Avoid any gaps in your rotation. You should always be casting a spell and Restoration is a very high APM healing spec. Any wasted time is time you could have spent casting Wrath to regenerate mana.

Further Explanation

In dungeon content, you will heal a combination of unavoidable and avoidable damage. The former you will be expected to heal through, the latter you will do what you can but ultimately aren't always responsible for. Restoration brings significant healing in Mythic+, which means you can heal through more mistakes than most other specs. Let's look at the healing abilities available to us:

Keep Efflorescence active at all times. If you are running Lifetreading (and the default build does) then keeping Lifebloom up does this for you. 
4Keep Lifebloom up at all times. This is crucial and Lifebloom will make up a lot of your dungeon healing via our Apex, Everbloom. 
Cast Swiftmend on cooldown, even if the party is reasonably healthy. It'll proc Power of the Archdruid which will put out two Rejuvenations, and Verdant Infusion will extend HoTs on your target.
2Cast Wild Growth during moderate damage periods, or to top the group up after minor damage. It's extremely GCD efficient, and also adds a Mastery stack to everyone in your group.
6React to anyone dropping very low with Nature's Swiftness + Regrowth, or just Regrowth depending on what is available.
7Fill any free time by contributing DPS. We'll cover that in detail below.

Breakdown & Explanation
Your key takeaway should be to take care of your maintenance tasks at all times (cooldown usage and uptimes mentioned above), and then use Regrowth as your primary healing button when people take damage. If you have time it's best to cast Rejuvenation on a few people prior to damage to make the group safer but this is very dependent on the scenario you find yourself in. Let's look through a few common dungeon scenarios.

Mythic+ often has a lot of short bursts that you'll have to handle as the Healer. Abilities like Alerting Shrill in Ara-kara where the damage is sharp and occurs over 3-6 seconds. These abilities are very telegraphed, so you'll know they're coming and have an opportunity to prep for them. Consider the following advice when countering them, and note that you'll only get 2-3 casts inside the actual damage windows:
Start prepping your party for the damage 5-6 seconds in advance. Eventually, as you grow more confident, you'll get away with committing fewer GCDs to each big damage event, but when starting out, play safe. Make sure Efflorescence is down, and that Lifeblooms is active.
Continue prepping by putting Rejuvenation on the group, prioritizing your DPS since Tanks aren't often phased by this type of AoE damage.
Cast Wild Growth as the boss begins its cast.
With Lifebloom on allies A, cast Swiftmend on B, and then cast Regrowth on whoever is most injured. Follow with further Regrowth casts to stabilize the group's Health.

You'll also have to handle a range of different, dangerous DoTs, but this section can also extend to Tank damage. With some mechanics, you'll get a few seconds to prepare but that's not guaranteed. If you're in a section of the dungeon with these, then it is worth keeping Lifebloom and Efflorescence active the entire pull. 
Cast 1-2 Rejuvenation on the target. It's not usually worth moving Lifebloom to a target since you'll lose all 3 stacks.
As the damage starts to tick, cast Swiftmend followed by Regrowth.
Follow up with more Regrowths, and use Nature's Swiftness if required.

Here's what you should do before every raid or dungeon:
Cast Mark of the Wild (our raid buff) - every pull.
Make sure Symbiotic Relationship is active on another player. Any squishy DPS player is a fine choice.
Make sure you have a Flask on - applied every 1-2 hours.
Make sure you have a Food buff - either every pull or every hour depending on the food.
Make sure you have a Thalassian Phoenix Oil on your weapon - applied every two hours.
(Optional) Make sure you have a Void-Touched Augment Rune on - every pull.
Start casting Rejuvenation a few seconds before the fight begins if there is relevant damage at the start. 

You can read about the best Flask and food buff to use in the Restoration Consumables guide.

 Restoration Druid Major Cooldowns

Restoration has access to some of the most powerful healing cooldowns in the game. Let's go through them and discuss where we might use them. Aim to pre-plan cooldowns as often as possible. Avoid scenarios where you're saving them "just in case", since this can cost you a lot of Mana through a fight and will increase the chance your raid suffers a death. Layer your raid's defensive cooldowns over the most dangerous moments of each fight to ensure you're covered.

 Tranquility 

Tranquility is our most powerful healing cooldown. It heals the entire raid or group for a significant amount and then extends all HoTs on the target by 2 seconds per Tranquility tick (10s overall - via the Flourish talent). You'll want to line up Tranquility with the most dangerous moments of the fight. You might even be assigned to use it at specific moments.

Playstyle-wise, you will want to change how you play in the lead-up to using Tranquility. Because the extension mechanic is so powerful we'll want to maximize how many effects we're extending. The most valuable heal-over-time effect to extend is Rejuvenation. It'll look a little something like this:

We will put out a Wild Growth and as many Rejuvenation buffs as possible, then extend them with Tranquility. That'll give us a wider window to spam cast free Regrowths afterwards with a 100% Crit chance. This is about a 20-25s window of healing in total and it is one of the biggest healing cooldowns in the game. If you take Incarnation: Tree of Life then it's often worth combining it with Tranquility because it'll actually pause the duration of your tree buff while you channel.

In Dungeons, Tranquility is used more for the healing it does by itself rather than its ramp / combo potential. Use it whenever the group is in danger.

 Convoke the Spirits 

Convoke the Spirits is a unique ability that casts 12-16 Druid abilities at random targets. The spells chosen have some logic to them but will mostly feel random. You can roughly expect:
0-2 Wild Growth casts
2-4 Swiftmend casts
4-5 non-resto casts like Wrath
A handful of Rejuvenation and Regrowth
A 50% chance of casting a single-tick-Tranquility (if you have the Cenarius' Guidance talent - this procs a two-second HoT extension as well if you have Flourish).

Convoke will also change its spells if you cast it in a different form. In Cat Form you will mostly get Cat-abilities, in Moonkin Form balance-abilities and so on. 

How to use it
In raid, we will always cast it in our regular caster form. We'll want to cast Rejuvenation beforehand since if we get the Flourish-extension then we'd like to get as much value out of that as possible. As mentioned in the rotation section above, a lot of our gameplay will revolve around ramping into these Convoke the Spirits or Tranquility casts. Follow Convoke with Regrowth casts regardless of whether you procced an extension or not. Convoke also gives us a lot of Grove Guardians because each Wild Growth or Swiftmend it includes will drop one. Our Convoke cast is a big healing moment.

In Mythic+, we'll cast Convoke in caster form if we need healing, and in Cat Form if we want to contribute more DPS. Its low cooldown gives us a lot of flexibility in our usage!

 Incarnation: Tree of Life 

Incarnation is our alternative to Convoke the Spirits and it focuses around increasing your healing for a longer period of time since Incarnation lasts a massive 30 seconds. You also get cooldown reduction for every Grove Guardian dropped so while it'll always be a longer cooldown than Convoke the Spirits, you can cast it about every 1:40 with good play. If you take Reforestation too then you can end up with 60-70% Incarnation uptime!

Incarnation: Tree of Life gives the following benefits while active, and any Rejuvenations you had out before you cast Incarnation will also benefit:
All healing increased by 10%.
Rejuvenation healing increased by 40%. Mana cost reduced by 30%.
Wild Growth hits 2 additional targets.
Wrath damage increased by 20%.
Regrowth is now instant-cast.

That's a decent package of power overall - particularly to Rejuvenation.

How to use it
You'll generally want to use Incarnation 10-12 seconds before major damage hits. That way you can take advantage of the massive discount to Rejuvenation. You can otherwise do your standard rotation while Incarnation is active. Note that its duration is paused while you're channeling Tranquility and combining the two is a good idea. Be careful that you do not overvalue the small Regrowth bonus - making it instant only front-loads the heal since its cast time is already equal to the global cooldown. 

 Druid Deep Dives

In this section, we'll cover different aspects of the spec in a little more depth. These are optional reads, but can be useful in increasing your overall understanding of the class. If you're brand new to the spec, I'd recommend getting some practice in first and then revisiting.

 Catweaving 

Catweaving is a way for us to contribute DPS where we swap to our Cat Form shapeshift and cast Cat Form abilities like Rake and Rip. It tends to be the highest DPS playstyle available to us in both raid and Mythic+, but it has a bit more complexity than just pressing Wrath with downtime so it gets its own section instead. You can generally master Restoration Druid healing first, and then start to incorporate Cat-gameplay once you're comfortable with the spec. 

Your DPS is not that important. At all times, make sure the party is comfortable first.

Cast Prowl before combat to get into stealth. This will also greatly buff our first ability cast.
Open with a Rake on the highest health enemy.
Continue applying rake to different enemies in the pack. When you have 5 combo points press Rip instead.
Once everyone has Rake, cast Swipe (3+ targets) or Shred (1-2 targets) instead.
On a single target, cast Ferocious Bite instead of Rip if the target already has one. 

Catweaving really boils down to "Apply Rake and Rip to as many targets as you can". You will want to have Rake (and optionally Shred) on your caster-form bar since that'll let you enter Cat Form automatically without spending a global cooldown (via Fluid Form). This also makes the playstyle flow much better.

It's very convenient for your Efflorescence to automatically drop under your Lifebloom target but if you're putting Lifebloom on the tank then you need to be slightly wary of where they are to make sure three+ people are in the Efflorescence. Feel free to place it on yourself for greater control if it's an issue.
You can refresh Lifebloom any time in the last 4.5 seconds of the buff to get the "bloom" effect, so you don't have to let it drop to maximize its healing.
